title: candidate-feedback-draft-sarah-johnson-2026-02-25
content:
Quick notes / scratchpad from loop with Sarah Johnson (L4 Backend). Draft for internal debrief.

Context:
- Role: L4 Backend Engineer (serving-runtime infra team)
- Stage: Technical loop (3x interviews) on 2026-02-25
- Interviewers: Samir (systems/design), Liam (coding), Evelyn (behavior + product sense)
- Candidate resume: 6 years infra experience, previous at mid-size infra startup, open-source contributions around RPC stack

Summary (high level):
- Strong systems intuition and distro-systems experience. Good at tradeoffs for latency vs throughput.
- Coding felt a bit rusty under time pressure; solved but needed hints on edge cases.
- Communication: clear, structured, asks good clarifying Qs. Team fit looks positive.

Scorecard (draft numbers — put on standard redwood rubric later):
- Technical breadth (systems + infra): 4/5
- System design (scalability, bottlenecks): 4/5
- Coding problem (algorithms + implementation): 3/5
- Communication / collaboration: 4/5
- Product sense / tradeoffs: 3.5/5
- Overall (rough): 3.5/5

Detailed notes by interviewer:
- Samir (systems/design):
  - Good on capacity planning, consistent hashing, cache invalidation patterns. Suggested nice idea for multi-tier KV cache with hot-key routing for low-latency paths.
  - Brought up cost/latency tradeoff explicitly which we like.
  - Weakness: didn't immediately consider cold-start latency in multi-tenant scenario until prompted.

- Liam (coding):
  - Problem: implement rate limiter + sliding-window approximation. Candidate outlined correct approach, implemented main loop but missed some concurrency edge cases (race on token bucket state).
  - Needed hint to use atomic ops / mutex. Implementation style OK but not idiomatic Go in places (uses slices where channels would be clearer).
  - Time management: spent too long on micro-optimizations instead of finishing full test cases.

- Evelyn (behavior + product sense):
  - Good stories about working with SREs to identify tail latency issues.
  - Culture fit: collaborative, prefers small cross-functional squads, invests in docs.
  - Concern: hasn't shipped infra at 100k qps scale personally (mostly at 30–40k).

Open questions / things to probe next loop:
- Real hands-on perf debugging example: want a concrete timeline where candidate found root cause (signal -> hypothesis -> experiment -> fix).
- Ownership examples where they drove cross-team rollout for breaking change (how did they mitigate risk?).
- Concurrency correctness under high throughput: ask for a walk-through of data structures used and failure modes.

Suggested next step / recommendation (draft):
- Move to onsite / final loop but with two adjustments:
  1) Include a focused concurrency/perf design + whiteboard where candidate walks through debugging and rollout plan for a hypothetical regression causing 2x tail latency.
  2) Consider a follow-up small take-home to validate correctness of concurrency handling (optional).
- Rationale: System design + product tradeoffs are strong; coding can be coached but we want higher confidence on concurrency correctness at scale.

Risks / cons:
- Coding under pressure may be a hiring risk for a role that sometimes needs quick bugfixes in production.
- Limited actual experience at 100k+ qps — may need ramp and mentorship.

Action items (Evelyn):
- Draft a short prompt for the onsite performance/debugging scenario (1 pager). Tag Samir + Liam for review.
- Add candidate to calendar for final loop (1.5–2h panel) if team agrees.
- Share this draft with Samir + Liam and convert scores to rubric in Greenhouse (or system we use) after signatures.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Follow up on GitHub samples: check PRs for concurrency patterns. Link above.
- Check references for production scale claims (ask specifically about qps numbers and incidents).

Unresolved:
- Salary expectation unclear — HR to confirm after we decide to proceed.
- Candidate mentioned they "prefer async communication" — verify will be OK with on-call rotations.

End of draft. Update after Samir / Liam add comments.
